newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council urges resumption of Mideast peace talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council urges resumption of Mideast peace talks.

text.p: With the United States abstaining, the Security Council called Saturday for the safety and protection of Palestinian civilians to be ensured and for the immediate resumption of the Middle East peace process.
The vote was 14 in favour and none against, with one abstention.

The resolution was the council's reaction to three days of bloody clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops which claimed nearly 70 lives following Israel's opening of a new entrance to an archaeological tunnel near the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
The resolution did not directly criticise Israel but it implicitly called for the closing of the tunnel entrance.

On Friday, Israel temporarily closed the tunnel, intended as a window for tourists on centuries of history along the Western, or Wailing Wall, Judaism's holiest shrine. But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Saturday the tunnel "has been around for 2,000 years...It will stay open."

During a daylong Security Council debate Friday, a succession of speakers criticised Israel's new right-wing government over the tunnel and accused it of dragging its feet on the peace process and of failing to implement agreements which the previous Labour-led government reached with the Palestinians.
